memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Now Cain said to his brother Abel, "Let's go out to the field." While they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him. - Gen 4:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The warning came, and Cain ignored it. The anger he refused to rule over grew until it drove him to lure his own brother into a field and kill him. What began as a downcast face ended in innocent blood. This is how sin works when we feed it instead of fighting it - it never stays the same size.

Jesus later traced murder back to its root: anger and contempt in the heart (Matt 5:21-22). Cain's hands did what his heart had already decided. That should sober all of us, because we may never lift a weapon, yet harbour the very bitterness that led Cain here.

This is a hard verse, and we should not soften it. It shows us the terrible reach of the fall - sin has moved from disobedience in a garden to murder in a field, and it is only the fourth chapter of the Bible.

But even this dark moment points forward. Abel's shed blood cries out for justice; the blood of Jesus "speaks a better word" - a word of forgiveness and mercy for guilty people like us (Heb 12:24). Where Cain brought death, Christ brings life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there anger you are quietly feeding today?
- Have you let bitterness take root against someone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart from the anger that destroys. Wash me in the blood of Jesus that speaks mercy over me.
